title.narrative: Amplify Asia - Media Development Investment Fund
Amplify Asia - Media Development Investment Fund

description.narrative:
MDIF is a not-for-profit investment fund for independent media in countries where access to free and independent media is under threat. Through a fund structure, MDIF invests in media partners from startup to growth-stage, providing affordable debt and equity financing to independent news and information businesses in a range of countries where access to free and independent media is under threat. MDIF also supports its portfolio media partners with specialist technical advice and assistance.
The primary purpose of the Amplify Asia programme is to strengthen the capacity of independent media in South and Southeast Asia by building their potential long-term sustainability to help them hold power to account and encourage the development of a well-informed and engaged civil society. The core components of the proposed programme are: coaching, specialist technical assistance, digital safety and security training and advice, gender mainstreaming and sub-grants. They will all be ongoing components throughout the five-year programme. The core of the programme is the provision of long-term business coaching to MDIF's media partners. While the coach works with the media partners on the development of an overall business strategy and various aspects of business development, some aspects of this require specialist help. The programme will provide this special technical assistance through the provision of the additional short-term specialist to address a particular need. The type of assistance can vary, from assistance to help with monetization of social media channels through to training on search engine optimization (SEO). Lastly, the sub-grants provision in the programme will allow MDIF to provide a modest funding pool that can be used to try out new business ideas of its media partners. These grants will be carefully integrated into the overall business capacity building work. Timeframes for the provision of digital safety and security assessments and training, as well as gender mainstreaming initiatives, will likewise be tailored to the specific needs of the media concerned. MDIF will hold an annual networking event for all media partners and their coaches and will also facilitate the participation by partners in regional conferences and peer-to-peer visits based on the needs and areas of focus of each media.

MDIF är en icke-vinstdrivande investeringsfond som fokuserar på mediaorganisationer i länder där tillgången till fri- och oberoende media är hotad. Genom en fondstruktur investerar MDIF i sina mediapartners från start till tillväxtfas, och tillhandahåller en överkomlig skuld- och aktiefinansiering till oberoende nyhets- och informationsföretag. Dessutom stödjer MDIF sina portföljmediapartners med specialiserad teknisk rådgivning och stöd.
Det primära syftet med det föreslagna programmet är att stärka kapaciteten hos oberoende medier i Syd- och Sydostasien genom att bygga upp deras potentiella långsiktiga hållbarhet och på så sätt hjälpa dem att hålla ansvarsbärare till svars, samt uppmuntra utvecklingen av ett välinformerat och engagerat civilt samhälle. De huvudsakliga komponenterna i det föreslagna programmet är: coachning och tekniskt specialiststöd , utbildning och rådgivning i digital säkerhet, jämställdhetsintegrering samt ett mindre finansiellt stöd. Kärnan i det femåriga programmet är att tillhandahålla långsiktig affärscoachning till MDIF:s mediapartners, och samarbeta med mediapartners för att utveckla en övergripande affärsstrategi och stärka olika aspekter av affärsutveckling. Programmet kommer att tillhandahålla denna specifika tekniska assistans inom områden som intäktsgenerering från sociala mediekanaler till utbildning i sökmotoroptimering (SEO). Slutligen kommer de mindre, finansiella bidragen att göra det möjligt för MDIF att tillhandahålla en blygsam finansieringspool som kan användas för att pröva nya affärsidéer för de mediaorganisationerna. Dessa anslag kommer noggrant att integreras i det övergripande arbetet, för att bygga upp verksamhetens kapacitet. Digitala säkerhets- och säkerhetsbedömningar och utbildningar samt initiativ för att integrering av ett jämställdhetsperspektiv kommer att anpassas till de berörda mediernas specifika behov, inklusive dess tidsramar. MDIF kommer att hålla ett årligt nätverksevenemang för alla mediepartners och deras mentorer/coacher, och kommer också att stimulera deltagandet av partners i regionala konferenser och peer-to-peer-besök, baserat på varje mediaorganisations behov och fokusområden.

The purpose of the programme is to strengthen the capacity of independent media in South and Southeast Asia by building their potential long-term sustainability to help them hold power to account and encourage the development of a well-informed and engaged civil society.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
In 2024, Amplify Asia's media partners saw a 78% audience growth and an outsized 290% revenue growth. This was directly due to coaching and capacity-building work from MDIF.
Recent examples of impact in Southeast Asia include the protests across Indonesia, where two media partners from different regions collaborated on hard hitting reporting that successfully cut through the flood of user generated content and online disinformation. During the program, an exiled Vietnamese media partner achieved a significant milestone, doubling its paid membership and substantially increasing reader revenue. Similarly, an Indonesian media partner tripled its revenue, both outcomes attributed to the tailored coaching provided through Amplify Asia.
One media partner in Sri Lanka serves a region where no other independent outlet operates, filling a critical gap in access to credible information. Another partner, based in Pakistan Hazara region a context marked by rampant drug trade and escalating extremism in recent months has made notable progress during its short time in the program. They have expanded their audience and revenue streams while launching an internship initiative primarily for young women who would otherwise have little opportunity to enter the media sector. In Nepal, recent protests were covered by two regional media partners who stood out as among the few reliable sources of news amid widespread misinformation. One media owner was interviewed by international outlets as a trusted voice on the ground.
The growth rates of both revenue and audience have exceeded the targeted indicators, showcasing MDIF's expertise and experience in effectively supporting media organizations in 2024 and 2025, despite limited human resources and a slow programme start.
